summary: Step M1-S04 of build tier2-webhook, owned by apex-builder, executed inline and set to 'built'. build_plan.py next listed the step, set-status running claimed it, the owning agent's Plan was run end to end under the artefact-path clause, check-outputs returned ok on all six declared outputs, and set-status built recorded the run against the owning agent's envelope. Five files landed that the plan did not declare - verbatim copies of ApplicationLogger.cls and TestDataFactory.cls with their meta XML, forced by apex-builder Step 6's provenance rule, plus deploy-order.md - which caps confidence at MEDIUM. The owning agent returned no refusal but a P0 finding: ApplicationLogger's own metadata prerequisites are shipped by no step of this build, so the package is not deployable until a human settles it at the M1 gate.
confidence_rationale: Step 9 MEDIUM row: five undeclared artefacts appeared under artefacts/M1-S04/, and two optional inputs of the owning agent (test_bulk_size, async_hint) had no value from any of the three Step 5 sources. Everything the HIGH row asks for otherwise held - the step was in next, every required input resolved from the plan, check-outputs exited 0, and no file was written outside artefacts/M1-S04/.

process_observations.observation: build_plan.py next, set-status and check-outputs each did exactly what the step needed and refused nothing, so no plan state was written by hand at any point in this run.
The step's three declared checkers each ran verbatim from the build directory and resolved through the skills symlink exactly as written, with no path substitution needed.

Noticed that a step's templates[] and outputs[] can disagree with no gate catching it: the provenance rule forces four files into the package that check-outputs will never confirm, and amend-step cannot fix it once the step has left pending.

evidence.query: section 2 amend-step preconditions vs section 4 Apex row note

process_observations.observation: Noticed that apex-builder has no build-layer contract at all - the AGENT.md grep for artefact/build_dir/step_id/.sfskills returns zero - so the artefact-path clause is honourable only because the owner was run inline rather than as a separate agent that would have persisted to its own default_output_dir.

The runner's Wave 10 persistence clause names docs/reports/build-step-runner/ while this invocation was constrained to write only under the build directory; both envelopes were written under the build directory only, which the envelope schema's build-layer path pattern permits.
The step is built and its declared tests have not been recorded by the agent that owns that record.
process_observations.followup_reason: because tests/M1-S04/results.json with passed:true is what gates the step's move from built to tested, and this agent never runs the step's acceptance tests.

process_observations.observation: Two findings on this step - the unmet logger prerequisite and the missing Apex foundations step - belong in the build's decisions log before the M1 gate.
process_observations.followup_reason: because it owns decisions.md and traceability.md, and a P0 deploy prerequisite discovered during a build is exactly the kind of decision the M1 gate has to see.
